origin_note: Most specialists place the early eighth-century adoption of Phoenician letters for Greek somewhere on Euboea; this is a regional attribution, not a claimed single workshop.

origin_label: Lower Danube / Moesia, fourth-century Gothic mission
origin_note: Wulfila developed the alphabet for Gothic Bible translation in the Greco-Roman world around the Black Sea and Lower Danube; a single creation site is not securely documented.
Mesrop Mashtots and Sahak introduced the alphabet in Armenia around 405; this point is a regional historical reference rather than a documented invention site.
The script is generally linked to the Christianization of Iberia/Kartli before its fifth-century attestations; exact origin and authorship remain contested, so this is a regional attribution.
